items.definition:
an approach that evaluates theories or beliefs in terms of the success of their practical application
His pragmatism helped him make difficult decisions.

the faith, practice, and church order of the Protestant churches
Protestantism is one of the major branches of Christianity.

the process of recombining things
Genetic recombination is a key process in evolution.

a movement in the arts and literature emphasizing inspiration, subjectivity, and the individual
Romanticism greatly influenced European art and music.

a large number of fish swimming together; a sandbank or sandbar
We saw a large shoal of fish near the coral reef.

an ancient symbol in the form of an equilateral cross with arms bent at right angles, used as a symbol of the Nazi party
The swastika is a symbol with a long and complex history, unfortunately associated with Nazism.

an animal with a backbone
Humans are vertebrates, as are fish, birds, and reptiles.

a direct opposite
Love is the antithesis of hate.

a very typical example of a certain person or thing
He is the archetype of a successful entrepreneur.

a deep fissure in the earth, rock, or another surface; a profound difference between people, viewpoints, feelings, etc.
A deep chasm opened up in the ground after the earthquake.

respect; humble submission
He showed great deference to his elders.

a disturbed state of mind
The patient was in a state of delirium due to the fever.

false information spread deliberately to deceive
The campaign was accused of spreading disinformation.

the front of a building; a deceptive outward appearance
The building's façade was beautifully decorated.

pointlessness or uselessness
He realized the futility of arguing with her.

a situation in which no progress is possible
Negotiations reached an impasse.

a sudden invasion or attack
There was a brief incursion into enemy territory.

the jaws or throat of a voracious animal
The lion opened its fearsome maw.

Nothing; zero.
All their efforts came to naught.

A regular periodic variation in magnitude or position.
The pendulum's oscillation was perfectly regular.

A device that produces oscillations.
An electronic oscillator is used to generate a repetitive waveform.

The quality of being easily shaped or molded.
The brain's plasticity allows it to adapt and learn throughout life.

the final section of the large intestine
The doctor examined the patient's rectum.

a repeated passage in music; a recurrence
The band played a short reprise of their hit song.

the saltiness of water or soil
The salinity of the ocean varies in different regions.

anal or oral sex
Laws against sodomy have been repealed in many countries.

the ability of a substance to dissolve in a solvent
The solubility of sugar in water increases with temperature.

a dry creek bed that fills with water after rain
After the heavy rain, the arroyo was flowing with water.

a small sensitive part of the female genitals
The clitoris is a highly sensitive organ.

a coal mine and its associated buildings
Many men in the village worked at the local colliery.

condemnation to eternal punishment in hell
He feared eternal damnation for his sins.

a person who disparages someone or something
Despite his detractors, he continued with his plan.

a person who believes in and promotes an idea or theory; a number or quantity representing the power to which a given number or expression is to be raised
She is a leading exponent of modern art.

strong criticism; publicity agent
The company received a lot of flack for its controversial advertising campaign.

a feudal lord or sovereign
The knight swore an oath of loyalty to his liege.

a mark placed over a vowel to indicate that it is long or stressed
The dictionary uses a macron to show long vowel sounds.

the condition of being diseased; the rate of disease in a population
The study examined the morbidity rates associated with the new virus.

an extinct species of human
Scientists have found many artifacts from Neanderthal communities.

a dark, glass-like volcanic rock
Ancient tools were often made from obsidian.

a member of a parliament; an expert in parliamentary procedure
The experienced parliamentarian guided the debate through complex rules.

ceremonial splendor and display
The royal wedding was conducted with great pomp and ceremony.

the result of a division; a degree or amount of a quality
In the division 10 ÷ 2 = 5, 5 is the quotient.

a period of paid leave for study or travel
She took a sabbatical from work to write a book.

a semi-liquid mixture, typically of fine particles suspended in a liquid
The cement mixer produced a thick slurry.

a genre of science fiction that has a historical setting and typically features steam-powered machinery
The novel is set in a steampunk version of Victorian London.

a taxonomic group that is a subdivision of a species
The Siberian tiger is a subspecies of tiger.

the action of adding something to complete or enhance something else
Vitamin D supplementation is often recommended in winter.

the process of designing and manufacturing tools
The company invested heavily in new tooling for the production line.

A soluble salt or base, typically one of the hydroxides of the alkali metals.
Sodium hydroxide is a strong alkali.

An indirect or passing reference.
The poem contained an allusion to Greek mythology.

a collection or gathering of things or people
The museum displayed an impressive assemblage of ancient artifacts.

the quality of being in accordance with a constitution
The court will rule on the constitutionality of the new law next month.

a plant variety that has been produced in cultivation by selective breeding
This new rose cultivar is resistant to common diseases.

a place where something is deposited or stored
The national archives serve as a depository for historical documents.

a small drink of whiskey or other spirits; a unit of weight
He poured himself a dram of whisky.

the study of the origin and history of words
The etymology of the word "hello" is quite interesting.

a person who expels evil spirits
The priest acted as an exorcist to help the troubled family.

excessive pride or self-confidence
His hubris led to his downfall.

security or protection against a loss or other financial burden
The company offered an indemnity against any losses.

The ability of computer systems or software to exchange and make use of information.
The new software greatly improved the interoperability between different departments.

The branch of science and technology concerned with the properties of metals and their production and purification.
He studied metallurgy to understand how metals behave.

The branch of metaphysics dealing with the nature of being.
Philosophy students often study ontology.

a small gland at the base of the brain
The pituitary gland plays a crucial role in hormone regulation.

a doubting or questioning attitude
There was widespread scepticism about the new proposal.
